question: What percentage of tests will be positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 4 (the Southeast) for the week ending October 17, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 4 (the Southeast) for the week ending 2026-10-17 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
I've pulled the CDC dataset and searched for news, so here is the report.

# RSV percent positivity, HHS Region 4, week ending 2026-10-17

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding data is CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb, Region 4, pathogen RSV, value as posted on 2026-10-30. I queried it through the Socrata API. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Latest values in the current file for weeks ending on or before 2026-09-05 (week ending: percent positive, number of tests):
  - 2026-09-05: 1.04% (5,020)
  - 2026-08-29: 0.67% (3,752)
  - 2026-08-22: 1.01% (4,372)
  - 2026-08-15: 0.57% (3,715)
  - 2026-08-08: 0.68% (3,509)
  - 2026-08-01: 0.69% (3,328)
  - 2026-07-25: 0.60% (3,344)
- Caveats:
  - The CDC usually posts each week's data several days after the week ends. As of 2026-09-07, the 2026-09-05 week may not have been public yet, so the latest visible point was probably 2026-08-29 at 0.67%.
  - The values I pulled are the current posted versions. Recent weeks can be revised.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The target week is about 6 weeks after the latest data.
- Region 4 RSV positivity has stayed between roughly 0.6% and 1.0% since mid-June 2026. The most recent week (1.04%, if it was public) hints at an early-season rise.
- The question's range tops out at 5.0%.

## 3. Recent news
- I found no dated CDC alert about RSV in the Southeast from August or September 2026, published by 2026-09-07. The Fox News and AJC "Southeast RSV rising" articles in my search results are undated or from earlier seasons. [Fox](https://www.foxnews.com/health/cdc-warns-increased-rsv-activity-southeastern-us.amp)
- Florida DOH publishes weekly RSV reviews. The week 34 report (Aug 23-29) came out in September 2026, but I couldn't read the PDF. Reports for later weeks were published after 2026-09-07, so I ignored them. [FL week 34](https://www.floridahealth.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/fl-rsv-review-week-34-2026.pdf)
- The 2025-26 Region 4 season peaked at 8.19% (week ending 2026-01-31). It fell below 2% by early May 2026. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 4. Base rates
Same dataset, Region 4, comparing early September with mid-October in past seasons:

| Season | Early Sept | Week matching Oct 17 | Rough multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 0.73% (09-06), 0.61% (08-30) | 2.01% (10-18); 1.83% (10-11), 2.84% (10-25) | about 2.7x |
| 2024 | 0.40% (09-07), 0.13% (08-31) | 4.88% (10-19); 2.01% (10-12), 3.78% (10-26) | large; week-to-week swings of 1-3 points |
| 2023 | 1.86% (09-09) | 10.72% (10-14) | about 6x |
| 2022 | 10.31% (09-10) | 13.59% (10-15) | unusual post-COVID early season |

- The 2025 path: 0.73 (09-06), 0.71, 1.04, 1.45, 1.38, 1.83, 2.01 (10-18).
- The 2024 path: 0.40 (09-07), 0.82, 1.80, 1.22, 3.07, 2.01, 4.88 (10-19).
- The two most recent seasons both started from about 0.4-0.7% in early September. They reached about 2% and about 4.9% in the matching mid-October week.
- 2026 starts in a similar place, at 0.67-1.04%.
- 2022 and 2023 had much earlier and larger fall seasons, partly because of post-pandemic timing.
- Since 2023, RSV prevention for infants (nirsevimab, maternal vaccine) and the RSV vaccines for older adults may have damped and delayed rises in positivity.
- Noise: in 2024, a single week moved by up to about 2.9 points in October. In 2025, weekly changes were about 0.1-0.8 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I didn't find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets on this series.
- I didn't search specifically for CDC's RSV season outlook or other modeling, and none turned up in my results.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The CDC posts NREVSS updates weekly, so there will be about 6 more data points (weeks ending 09-12 through 10-10) before the target week.
- The target-week value will first appear around 2026-10-23. The question resolves on the version posted 2026-10-30, which may include revisions.
- Things that could move the number:
  - Whether the Southeast season starts as early as usual (Florida and Georgia typically lead the country).
  - How many infants get nirsevimab, clesrovimab or the maternal vaccine during 2026-27.
  - Changes in the number of tests, since more testing of mildly ill people could lower positivity.
